label: SYNTHETIC READER: a test instrument, never a reader. Fictional; not evidence about the book; not readership.

findings.quote: I did not have to explain the movement.
findings.why: The building is told here, then again as a still slide with its narration (lines 69-73) and again in a figure, so the scene is said three times.

findings.quote: Four sentences of narration, for one picture
findings.why: It reads out the count of the paragraph just given, which the reader can already see.

findings.quote: It was one of those loops I would have stopped before.
findings.why: I could not tell what loop, or why he would have stopped it; as a builder I want the failure mode named.

findings.quote: Wardley maps are the best thing I have learned in the last decade
findings.why: A claim of enthusiasm with no map shown or explained in a line, so the reader has to take it on trust.

findings.quote: You will see this kind of map again in part two
findings.why: I have not yet been told how the book is divided, so 'part two' points at nothing.

findings.quote: If you have one you keep explaining by hand, try writing that movement down in a single line.
findings.why: The closing card is three one-line sentences in a row, each its own italic paragraph.
An instruction on how to value the talk rather than a reason given.

findings.quote: The clock below shows the last of them.
findings.why: Points at a figure instead of saying something the figure does not.

findings.quote: it landed twelve minutes later, seven minutes before I stopped everything
findings.why: The same ask, twelve minutes and seven minutes are in the figure caption at line 23, so the numbers are read out twice.

findings.quote: looking back I think it says something good: this project never needed one
findings.why: A newsroom builder wants a source for 'never needed a security agent' and gets an opinion, in a book whose later chapters are about containing the team.

findings.quote: Nothing was created, nothing was scheduled. It waited for me to say yes.
findings.why: A run of short sentences where one longer thought would carry the signature as the control.

findings.quote: The build every change goes through is mine.
findings.why: 'The gate' appears in the card and is only explained in the next paragraph (line 71), and 'build' and 'check' are used as if known.

findings.quote: Pushing to the main branch: an expectation.
findings.why: 'Main branch' and the difference between an expectation and a setting are not explained, and this is the passage I most wanted to understand.

findings.quote: That is the weight I want you to see.
findings.why: It tells the reader what to see, and the 2,666 count carries no stated source on the page.

what_holds: 01-slides-as-a-compromise.md: the figure caption admitting the page said all ten policies while the files say eight of ten; a builder who wants the record behind every line trusts it.
02-inventing-on-principle.md: 'I am not going to pretend the day lived up to that' corrects the grand claim in the same breath.
04-hour-one-the-empty-project.md: the reality file rule, 'A thing not listed here does not exist', and the page of rules read as lessons learned, are what I would copy tomorrow.
notes: As a newsroom builder I would start with the conductor-style role and the page of rules. The editor's signature is shown as approving, changing or questioning, which answers the rubber-stamp worry in chapter 1; chapter 4 only says the team waited for a yes.
